category: software-defined S3 object storage on user-run storage nodes (self-hosted; Coordinator managed by Cubbit or self-hosted)

free_tier.stated: Up to 3 TB of DS3 Composer free tier access at 0 EUR, no credit card required; the storage itself sits on nodes the user supplies
free_tier.notes: a licence for software, not capacity that Cubbit hosts: the pricing FAQ licenses Composer on raw installed capacity, and every stored byte uses disks the user provides. unverified: whether the 3 TB is counted on raw or usable capacity. Above the free tier the rate is EUR 4.99 per TB per month for 3 to 10 TB, discounted above 10 TB.

per_object_cap.stated: unverified: no Composer page states an object-size limit
per_object_cap.notes: the DS3 multipart-upload page lists a 5 TiB maximum object size for Cubbit's S3 gateway; whether Composer gateways share it is not stated.

retention.stated: unverified: no Cubbit page states a duration or an expiry for the 3 TB free tier
retention.notes: the only duration on the pricing page, 30 days, belongs to the hosted DS3 Cloud demo, a separate record. The marketplace listing calls the Composer free tier a free trial with no duration. Licence expiry and grace terms are in the customer contract, which is not public.

egress.terms: Cubbit charges no egress, deletion, bucket replication or API fee under its flat per-TB rate; the Cubbit-run public gateway's egress is free for now and may change; bandwidth of the user's own nodes and gateways is the user's own

interface_detail: S3-compatible API exposed by a DS3 Gateway: a public gateway per tenant that Cubbit runs, or a private gateway the user installs on a Kubernetes cluster
tooling: A hosted S3 offer from Cubbit is the separate DS3 Cloud record; this record is the software. The user installs and runs one Cubbit storage agent per disk on Linux machines (1 CPU thread and 1 GB of RAM per disk) registered as nodes in a Swarm, on a rented or free machine; the Coordinator control plane is Cubbit-managed (composer.cubbit.eu) or a licensed self-hosted install; S3 access goes through a Cubbit-run public gateway or a private gateway the user installs on a Kubernetes cluster. Clients: AWS CLI and other S3 clients.
chaining: A hosted S3 origin from Cubbit is the DS3 Cloud record (1 TB, 30-day trial); this record gives no hosted capacity. Its 3 TB licence is only useful on disks the user rents or already has, three servers at least per the marketplace listing, so it chains with capacity from other records and adds no storage of its own.

limits.value: up to 3 TB on the free tier; EUR 4.99 per TB per month from 3 to 10 TB
entry through a form asking for a work email, company name and an organisation-size answer; the documentation calls access invite-only

limits_note: Licensing counts raw installed capacity (pricing FAQ). A Swarm starts from three servers (marketplace listing, trade report) and each disk needs 1 CPU thread and 1 GB of RAM; the vendor positions Composer from 200 TB upward.
binding_note: the free tier is entered through a form that asks for a work email and a company name and the documentation describes access as invite-only; the 3 TB is also a licence on machines the user must supply

identity_cost.detail: The free-tier form asks for a work email, first name, last name, company name and country, then a required yes or no on whether the organisation uses more than 50 TB, with an optional phone number; no credit card is asked. The documentation says DS3 Composer is invite-only, with an emailed invitation to a pre-generated account, and that page was last updated on 22 February 2024. unverified: whether Cubbit approves an entry whose company is not a registered business; the form was read and not submitted.

reliability_note: no throttle, suspension or data-loss event is stated on the pages read; licence expiry and grace terms are in the customer contract, which is not public. unverified: what a Swarm does when the free-tier licence ends.
confidence_note: every fact is quoted from Cubbit pages read on 2026-11-03; the free-tier form was read and not submitted, so the approval rule and the free tier's duration are not published and stay unverified.
